refuter.evidence: rep_pt2sep.cob at --std 85: pseudo-text-2 of only a separator comma and of only a semicolon (SR7 limits only pseudo-text-1) were accepted and substituted (ADD 1 TO WS-A, WS-B printed 0011 and 0021). A nonnumeric literal in pseudo-text-2 continued onto a continuation line (SR5) gave 'ABCDEFGHIJ- ' in X(12), correct because the literal runs to margin R. A pseudo-text-2 holding a debugging line was accepted. Every form SR4 admits compiles. LEAD, under another rule and not this verdict: with no WITH DEBUGGING MODE, the DISPLAY that REPLACE inserts from a D line in pseudo-text-2 EXECUTES. rep_dbg_ctl.cob printed VIA-REPLACE / END, while a direct D line in the same program stays a comment. The COPY twin copy_dbg_ctl.cob (COPY DBGLIB REPLACING ==DBG-ONE== BY ==<D line DISPLAY>==) correctly prints only END. The REPLACE path drops the debugging-line status of pseudo-text-2 text, against §1985:XII.3.4 GR7/GR8 read with the COPY GR9 placement, and kb/Work PB5382 (landed) claims both twins. At --std 2023 the D line itself is refused (COBOL0902). cite.py: OK  §1985:XII.3.3 SR4  (║3.3 Syntax Rules║)  the text is in SR4; OK  §1985:XII.3.4 GR7  (║3.4 General Rules║)  the text is in GR7.
